title: His father's upbringing and Blakeney's schooling
summary: His father was raised by a white family and became a teacher; Blakeney starts school in 1903 and quits after the seventh or eighth grade.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: My father was born in Quitman, Mississippi, November 29, 1864. The year before the surrender he always told it. He was the youngest of seven. At four years old his mother passed, not knowing who or what his father was; a white family took him in in their home.

The wife, a Mistress Bailey, taught him to read and write. At the age of twelve or thirteen he had to leave the white family and he started living with his older brothers and their children, who were about his same age.
He continued to study and had plenty of books. After he was grown and out on his own, his first job naturally was

teaching school.
I first attended school September, 1903. My papa took me to that one room school on the back of a mule and delivered me to Professor McGowan. I breezed through all grades up to the seventh, kind of lonely because I was the only big boy in school. All the other families kept their boys home to help on the farm.
Papa wouldn't let me go to Meridian so I could finish school, so I quit that eighth grade school where I knew almost as much as the teachers.
